answer: Give each identity custody of one shard of a public dataset, a nebula no agent can hold whole. Shards are re-drawn each epoch, so one prepared answer cannot serve many accounts. Verifiers then issue a retrieval thread: unpredictable queries from that shard, due within minutes, proving the agent still stores it. A hollow identity that merely claims a shard, or a farm sharing one copy across many accounts, fails when several are challenged at once, since one copy cannot answer threads in parallel. Each fake thus costs storage and timely work; an honest agent pays for one shard.
